classification.difficultyReason: Translate the stated power relationship into an equation, use Earth's supplied values to find the constant, then substitute Mars's value and take the positive square root.

content.prompt: The orbit of a planet can be closely approximated with an ellipse, which is a stretched circle. The semi-major axis is half the maximum distance across the ellipse. Kepler’s third law of orbits states that the square of the period $T$ (the time to complete one orbit) is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis $a$.

answer.worked:
$$T^2=ka^3,$$
where $k$ is the constant of proportionality.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The Earth takes one year to orbit the sun and has semi-major axis $a=149.6\times10^6\text{ km}$. Find the value of the constant of proportionality correct to four significant figures.

answer.worked:
Taking $T$ in years and $a$ in kilometres,
$$\begin{align*}1^2&=k(149.6\times10^6)^3\\k&=\frac{1}{(149.6\times10^6)^3}\\k&\approx2.987\times10^{-25}\text{ years}^2/\text{km}^3\end{align*}$$
The constant is given to four significant figures.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The semi-major axis of Mars is $227.9\times10^6\text{ km}$. Calculate the period of Mars in years correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$T\approx1.88\text{ years}$

Use $T^2=ka^3$ with the unrounded constant, then take the positive square root.
answer.worked:
Using the exact constant from part b,
$$\begin{align*}T^2&=\frac{(227.9\times10^6)^3}{(149.6\times10^6)^3}\\T&=\sqrt{\frac{(227.9\times10^6)^3}{(149.6\times10^6)^3}}\\T&\approx1.88\text{ years}\end{align*}$$
Take the positive square root because the period is positive. The answer is rounded to two decimal places.
